comments.author: uweigand
comments.body:
Hi @JonPsson1, looks like you added this code here: https://reviews.llvm.org/D97514

The problem is that
```
        EVT OrigArgVT = getValueType(MF.getDataLayout(), OrigArgType);
```
doesn't work if the original argument type is a struct like in this case.

Maybe we should avoid looking at the original type after all, and simply compute the required space from the list of parts (we know where we're going to store them, so we should be able to just track the space requirements).

Can you have a look?

comments.author: JonPsson1
comments.body:
I see in the ABI:

```
• Structures with a size of 1, 2, 4, or 8 bytes which are not equivalent to a floating
point type are passed as integral values.
• All other structures are passed by reference. If needed, the called function makes a
copy of the value.

```

If I can compile a C program and pass a struct containing just an __int128, clang emits that argument as a pointer (per above), both in the declaration of called function and at the call site.

So I actually wonder if the test case is legal - meaning if so that the backend would have the responsibility of converting everything to match the ABI, which would be really awkward given that this also includes transforming function declarations etc. I don't see in the lang-ref ('call' instruction) anything that specifies this, though.

comments.author: alexrp
comments.body:
It is true that Zig doesn't handle the s390x ABI correctly here, and that's a bug in Zig.

However, that's actually immaterial to this issue; LLVM IR is not C, and it's expected that `call`s involving types not covered by the C ABI are still lowered to something semantically sensible, even if that doesn't match the C ABI. It's then the frontend's responsibility not to rely on that at C ABI boundaries (again, *that* aspect is a bug in Zig).

Note that this crash also occurs if you change `ccc` to `fastcc`.

comments.body: @alexrp Does this resolve your issue regarding this?

comments.body: Judging by the test case added, I believe so. Thank you!
